audit_findings.title: The valuation mixes three different acquisition perimeters
audit_findings.magnitude: $424.5 million paid for LKC and First Aviation through June 2026; Indicor consideration approximately $5.0 billion, annual sales approximately $1.1 billion, and committed acquisition facilities up to $5.0 billion; Indicor consideration equals 15.9% of the $31.378 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The 2025 OE anchor excludes 2026 acquisitions, the June 2026 cash and debt bridge includes LKC and First Aviation, and the post-Indicor common-equity claim would include acquired earnings, financing costs, cash usage, debt and any dilution on another perimeter.
audit_findings.evidence: In January 2026, the Company acquired LKC Technologies, a leading provider of innovative technology to enable effective diagnosis and management of ophthalmic conditions.
audit_findings.explanation: A perimeter mismatch is demonstrated: the earnings anchor and balance-sheet bridge do not describe the same owned businesses. Indicor's exact post-closing effect remains unresolved, but its filed $5.0 billion scale is reasonably capable of changing the valuation. Acquired earnings could raise value while financing costs, integration spending and reduced cash could lower it, so direction is mixed.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the post-Indicor closing balance sheet, consideration and financing details, assumed liabilities, awards or shares, and acquired-company earnings; construct post-closing trailing OE including LKC, First Aviation and Indicor, then rerun every scenario and the bridge on that single perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition-driven growth may be treated as free growth
audit_findings.magnitude: 15 acquisitions with approximately $1.8 billion of annualized sales during 2021-2025; 2025 acquisition spending was $933.2 million, while acquisitions supplied 4 percentage points of 2025's 6.6% sales growth; net valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Forecast growth increases OE without an explicit deduction for the acquisition consideration and integration reinvestment required to obtain acquired growth.
audit_findings.evidence: Since the beginning of 2021 through December 31, 2025, AMETEK has completed 15 acquisitions with annualized sales totaling approximately $1.8 billion.
audit_findings.explanation: The historical dependence on acquisitions and the exclusion of business purchases from OE are demonstrated. Whether the 7% and 10% forecasts are intended to be wholly organic is unresolved. Because 2025 acquisition spending equaled 52.9% of the $1,763.5 million OE anchor and most reported 2025 sales growth came from acquisitions, a recurring uncharged acquisition requirement is reasonably capable of materially overstating value.
audit_findings.action: Decompose historical sales and OE growth into organic and acquired components; rerun each scenario either using supportable organic growth alone or deducting a normalized after-tax acquisition, integration and incremental working-capital requirement consistent with the assumed growth.

audit_findings.title: Required working-capital investment may be missing from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 OE exceeded filed free cash flow by $91.9 million, or 5.2% of anchor OE; 2025 receivable, inventory/other-current-asset and payable/accrual/tax movements used a computed $133.4 million of cash; normalized effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If accrual-based OE omits recurring increases in receivables and inventory net of operating liabilities, OE and forecast distributable cash are overstated as sales grow.
audit_findings.evidence: The decrease in cash provided by operating activities for 2025 was primarily due to higher working capital investments, partially offset by higher net income.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates material working-capital cash use in 2025, but the record does not establish the precise OE reconciliation or how much of that use is recurring, organic, acquisition-related or timing-related. First-half 2026 also reported reduced working-capital investment, so one period cannot establish a normalized charge. If the $91.9 million OE-to-free-cash-flow gap recurred, the proportional base-value effect would be about $1.61 billion or $6.94 per share, but recurrence is not demonstrated.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every OE year to operating cash flow; isolate acquisition-date balances and unusual timing; estimate normalized incremental operating working capital per dollar of organic sales, then rerun the DCF with that charge tied to each growth scenario.

audit_findings.title: Customer advances may make the cash add-back non-surplus
audit_findings.magnitude: June 2026 contract liabilities were $502.973 million versus $495.446 million of cash; eliminating the entire cash add-back would reduce base value by $2.14 per share, from $135.25 to approximately $133.11, or 1.6%
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash funded by advance billings may be operating liquidity needed to fulfill prepaid obligations rather than surplus cash available for addition to equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: For the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, the Company recognized revenue of $ 328 million and $ 359 million, respectively, that was previously included in the beginning balance of contract liabilities.
audit_findings.explanation: The existence of contract liabilities exceeding cash is demonstrated, but the filing does not trace particular cash dollars to customer advances or establish that all cash is restricted operationally. Even the conservative maximum adjustment of removing the full cash add-back changes base value by only 1.6% and does not alter the valuation conclusion relative to the $237.70 market price.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a June 2026 sources-and-uses analysis for cash, contract liabilities and required operating liquidity; retain only demonstrably surplus cash in the bridge, while ensuring fulfillment costs and contract-liability working capital are not counted twice.

audit_findings.title: Accrued tax claims are absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $247.9 million of tax, interest and penalties classified as a non-current liability at December 2025; June 2026 gross uncertain tax benefits were $243.3 million; a full $247.9 million deduction equals approximately $1.07 per share or 0.8% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash settlement of previously accrued tax claims may reduce the residual common-equity bridge without reducing future accrual-based OE if the corresponding expense was already recognized.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, tax, interest and penalties of $ 247.9 million were classified as a non-current liability and $ 4.6 million was reflected as a reduction against deferred tax assets.
audit_findings.explanation: The liability and its omission from the stated bridge are demonstrated, although the eventual settlement amount, timing and amount already represented in forecast taxes remain unresolved. A conservative deduction of the entire filed $247.9 million would reduce base value by only about 0.8% and would not change the conclusion relative to the market price.
audit_findings.action: Update tax, interest and penalty accruals to the valuation date; estimate expected cash settlements and identify amounts already captured in OE tax expense; deduct only the non-duplicative expected settlement from the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Deferred compensation can settle in cash or uncounted shares
audit_findings.magnitude: $40.6 million filed obligation at December 2025; full cash deduction equals approximately $0.18 per share or 0.13% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash settlement is an equity-bridge claim, while share settlement increases the fully diluted denominator if the potential shares are not already included.
audit_findings.evidence: The amount owed to participants is an unfunded and unsecured general obligation which is payable out of either the general assets of the Company or a grant of shares of the Company's common stock.
audit_findings.explanation: The obligation is demonstrated, but its settlement form and inclusion in diluted shares are unresolved. Even treating the full filed balance as an additional cash claim reduces base equity value by only 0.13%, far too little to change the valuation conclusion. Share dilution could differ with the settlement price, but the liability's filed scale remains small.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the latest liability, participant elections, share-conversion terms and maximum issuable shares; record it once, either as a bridge deduction or additional dilution, and verify that it is not already included in the 231.997244 million-share denominator.
